title: Dock
summary: A workspace of panels (Toolbox | Canvas | Properties) laid out as a tree of resizable splits and tab groups. Drag a separator or use its arrow keys to resize, choose a tab to switch a group, or use a single-panel header's chevron to collapse it to just its title. The arrangement is one JSON layout document you can read, store and set. Docked panels and header-collapse only; moving panels, floating and saved layouts come in later steps of #432.

props.name: layout
props.description: The arrangement: { version, seq, root, collapsed } where root is a split { id, type: 'split', orientation, size, min, max, a, b } or a tab group { id, type: 'tabs', active, panels }, and collapsed is the list of open panel ids folded to their header. Leave it unset for the default arrangement derived from each panel's data-group. The element validates what it is given (panels that are not declared are dropped, panels the layout lacks are added, bad numbers are repaired). While the user resizes, chooses a tab or collapses a panel the element owns it; after pk-layout-change the host does. Property or a JSON attribute.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of a tab group (aria-label), for example the workspace's name. A single-panel group is named by its heading.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of every separator between two panels (aria-label).

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill the height the parent gives it (a parent with a definite height, or a flex or grid parent) instead of --pk-dock-height.

props.name: persistKey
props.description: Save and restore the layout across reloads, through the SDK's store (js/store.js), under the key pk-dock:<persistKey>. Leave unset to disable persistence. On connect, a saved layout is used as the initial arrangement when the layout prop is not set (stored data wins over the default arrangement); every later pk-layout-change (resize, activate, panels) is saved, but a layout the host sets is not. Give each pk-dock on a page its own value; changing it starts a fresh, separately-saved layout.

slots.name: <panel id>
slots.description: One panel: any element with slot="<id>" (a lowercase id, letters, digits, - and _, up to 40 characters). data-heading is its title (the id when missing) and data-group (left, center, right, bottom) places it in the default arrangement. Panels are slotted, never moved, so a form or a scroll position inside one survives resizing and switching tabs.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Shown when there is no panel.

events.name: pk-layout-change
events.description: The arrangement changed because of the user or because panels were added or removed: reason is resize (a drag ended or a key moved a separator), activate (a tab was chosen), collapse (a single-panel header's chevron toggled its body) or panels (the declared panels changed and the layout was repaired). layout is the new document. Not raised for a layout the host set, nor for the first render. Not cancelable.

parts.name: root
parts.description: The frame that holds the rendered tree.

parts.name: group
parts.description: One tab group or single panel, with its header.

parts.name: header
parts.description: The title bar of a single-panel group.

parts.name: collapse-toggle
parts.description: The button in a single-panel header that collapses or expands its body.

parts.name: title
parts.description: The panel's heading text inside collapse-toggle.

parts.name: body
parts.description: The scrolling area around a panel's content.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-height
cssProperties.description: Height when fill is not set.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-header-height
cssProperties.description: Minimum height of a single-panel header.

a11y: Each separator is a pk-splitter: role=separator with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and its own arrow keys (Left and Right side by side, mirrored in a right-to-left page; Up and Down stacked; Home and End), so every resize has a keyboard path. A group of several panels is a pk-tabs tablist (roving tabindex, arrow keys); a single panel is a labelled section named by its heading. Hidden tab panels are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree. A single-panel header's collapse-toggle is a native button (Tab to reach it, Enter or Space to activate, no extra key handling needed) with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the body it hides; a tab group does not offer collapse yet.
mobile: Below 640px a splitter tree cannot show real panels, so the dock draws every open panel in reading order as one tab strip with one panel visible; the strip scrolls sideways rather than wrapping onto a second row, the same as a narrow group's tab list. The layout document is untouched, so widening the window restores the arrangement.
